object_entity.proposition_label: Christ the Logos is the pre-existent Son of God
object_entity.description: The Word/Logos of God, who became incarnate as Jesus Christ, pre-existed creation as the Son and mind of the Father, through whom all things were made.

context_place.notes: Central region between Judea and Galilee associated with Acts 8 mission activity.

evidence.notes: Passage contextualizes simon-magus's position on logos-is-pre-existent-son-of-god.

passage.excerpt: Now for some time a man named Simon had practised sorcery in the city and amazed all the people of Samaria. He boasted that he was someone great... Philip proclaimed the Christ; Simon himself believed and was baptized. When Simon saw that the Spirit was given at the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money, saying 'Give me also this ability.' But Peter answered: 'May your money perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money.'

source.title: Acts of the Apostles
source.author: Traditionally Luke
source.notes: Narrative witness for the apostolic expansion beyond Judea.

evidence.notes: Irenaeus AH 1.26.2: Ebionites reject the pre-existent Logos, affirming Jesus as mere man.

passage.excerpt: Those called Ebionites agree that the world was made by God; but their opinions with respect to the Lord are similar to those of Cerinthus and Carpocrates. They use the Gospel according to Matthew only, and repudiate the Apostle Paul, maintaining that he was an apostate from the law. As regards the prophetical writings, they endeavour to interpret them in a singular manner. They practise circumcision and observe the Mosaic law. They affirm Jesus was the son of Joseph and Mary.

passage.excerpt: Simon the Samaritan was that magician of whom Luke, the disciple and follower of the apostles, writes in Acts. He claimed to be the supreme divine Power, the father of all heresy. Having purchased a certain woman named Helena, he declared her to be the first Conception of his mind, the mother of all, through whom he had originally conceived the creation of angels and archangels.
